findings.text: blocking: snapshot_if_due accepts any same-day filename without verification, so a damaged newest file suppresses further snapshots that day despite the verified-daily-copy requirement.
blocking: watch_publish.py:116 can read an old watch.json through this fallback and write it back with a new published_at at watch_publish.py:119, falsely presenting stale measurements as fresh.
follow-on: PUBLISHED_WATCH_PATH duplicates watch_publish.DEFAULT_OUTPUT at watch_publish.py:39 and can drift from the producer's path.

follow-on: the explicit-path assertion compares the returned path with the same path supplied to the resolver; a mere echo passes without proving validation, so the locality refusal must be judged by the separate injected-network assertion.
follow-on: the retention assertions use only valid snapshots, so pruning by filename rather than by verified copies would also keep three files and pass.

follow-on: baseline_suite and after_suite are empty, leaving no structured suite-delta receipt even though placement-and-cli-tests.log and final-placement-gate.log both report 16 passed and no failure ids.
